_doc: clinic-scan — a person with two switches types their own name into the patient card (2026-09-03).
Switch scanning: the keyboard sweeps rows then keys; 'select' (thumbs up / a switch / Space) picks,
'back' (fist / Escape) steps out. Under ?test=1 the sweep is frozen (window.__cedarfieldScanMs) so
the run is deterministic; the on-screen Select/Back controls and real key presses drive it. A real
hand shape cannot be faked here; the switch mapping is unit-tested in scan-keyboard.test.ts and the
sign channel routing (routeSign) is exercised by the last steps through the same sink the camera uses.
Open the scanning keyboard for the full name. The sweep is frozen on row 0 (a–g).
Select row 0, then select key 0: 'a' is typed and the sweep returns to rows.
A hardware switch or the space bar is the same select: Space, Space types another 'a'; Escape mid-row steps out; Backspace at rows deletes.
Codex re-audit 2026-09-03: Escape must step back even while focus sits on the keyboard's own Select button.
The camera's sign channel goes to the keyboard while it is open, not to the request queue: a thumbs-up routed through the same sink selects; a palm does nothing.

eval: (() => { const live = document.querySelector('[data-clinic-listen-pending]')?.textContent ?? ''; window.__pendingBefore = live; return true; })()

_doc: The screen reader line names what is highlighted.
Close the keyboard: the field keeps the typed text, the offer returns, and Save still needs the person.

Hands-free (2026-09-03): with the card open and no keyboard, one finger opens the keyboard on the next EMPTY field (the name holds 'a', so the date); thumbs down closes it; done on the last field saves. The seam window.__cedarfieldSign(category) delivers a shape exactly where the camera would.

Fill the name and date by keyboard (a real keyboard is a switch too), leave the phone empty; one finger opens the keyboard on the phone; a fast sweep (400 ms, test hook) reaches the last row; done on the last empty field saves the card.

_doc: Saved by hand shapes alone: the card is on file and the shapes go back to the request queue (a thumbs-up now is 'yes', not a switch).

Digits for the phone: open the keyboard on the phone field; rows 4–5 hold 0–9. Select row 0? No: the sweep is frozen on row 0, so a real run waits for the sweep; here only the open/close contract is asserted.
